h: Sanctifying Every Aspect of Ordinary Life

p: סְעוּדָה שְׁלִישִׁית דְּשַׁבָּת חָשַׁב רַבִּי יִצְחָק לוּרְיָא זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
— The Ari, of blessed memory, reckoned the third Shabbat meal as corresponding to the sanctity of Jacob our father, peace be upon him.
וּמָצִינוּ אֶצְלוֹ שֶׁעָשָׂה סְעוּדָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיִּזְבַּח יַעֲקֹב זֶבַח בָּהָר וְגוֹמֵר וַיֹּאכְלוּ לָחֶם.
— We find that Jacob made a feast: “Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain,” and so forth, “and they ate bread.”
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין מַה הָיָה עִנְיַן הַסְּעוּדָה שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי לֹא עָשָׂה סְעוּדַת הָרְשׁוּת,
— We must understand this feast, for certainly he did not make a merely optional feast.
וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א׳ קמב ב) תָּא חֲזֵי יַעֲקֹב כָּל עוֹבָדוֹי הֲווֹ לִשְׁמָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵי.
— The holy Zohar (I, 142b) teaches: “Come and see: all Jacob’s deeds were for the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He,” and so forth.

h: Gilead and the Boundary of Holiness

p: אָכֵן גִּלְעָד הָיָה הַהֶבְדֵּל בֵּין חוּץ לָאָרֶץ לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ וַיִּפְגְּעוּ בוֹ מַלְאֲכֵי אֱלֹהִים וּפֵרֵשׁ רַבִּי שְׁלֹמֹה יִצְחָקִי מַלְאָכִים שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵי,

— Gilead marked the boundary between outside the Land and the Land of Israel. As it says afterward, “Angels of God encountered him”; Rashi explains that these were angels of the Land of Israel, and so forth.
וְגִלְעָד הוּא קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ שֶׁמַּקִּיף וְסָמוּךְ לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
— Gilead corresponds to kelippat nogah, the mixed husk of radiance, which surrounds and borders the Land of Israel.
וְאִיתָא (מְגִילָּה ט׳.) תַּרְגּוּם שֶׁכְּתָבוֹ מִקְרָא וְכוּלֵי אִיכָּא יְגַר שָׂהֲדוּתָא וְנִצְרָךְ לְכָתְבוֹ תַּרְגּוּם דַּיְיקָא.
— It is taught in Megillah 9a, “Aramaic that one wrote in Hebrew,” and so forth: there is the phrase yegar sahaduta, which must specifically be written in Aramaic.
וּבְסֵפֶר מְגַלֶּה עֲמֻקּוֹת אִיתָא שֶׁנִּרְמַז עִנְיַן חַשְׁמוֹנָאִים בְּתֵיבַת יְגַר שֶׁהָיָה שְׁנַת רי״ג לִתְחִלַּת בִּנְיַן בַּיִת שֵׁנִי,
— The book Megaleh Amukot teaches that the Hasmonean events are alluded to in yegar, whose letters total 213, for it was in the 213th year from the beginning of the Second Temple’s construction,
(וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵדֶר עוֹלָם רַבָּה וְעַיֵּן סֵדֶר הַדּוֹרוֹת) שֶׁאָז הָיָה הַגְּזֵירָה וְנִתְגַּבְּרוּ עַל הַיְּוָנִים וְיַעֲקֹב תִּקְּנוֹ שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ גַּלְעֵד.
— (as stated in Seder Olam Rabbah; see Seder Hadorot) that the decree occurred and they overcame the Greeks. Jacob rectified it by calling it Gal-ed.

וְהָעִנְיָן דְּאִיתָא (בַּזֹּהַר חָדָשׁ פָּרָשַׁת יִתְרוֹ ד״ו לח סוֹף עַמּוּד א׳) נֹגַהּ לוֹ סָבִיב דָּא אִיהוּ מַלְכוּת יָוָן דְּסַחֲרָא לוֹן נוֹגַהּ וְכוּלֵי בְּגִין דְּלֵית בְּכָל מַלְכְוָון דְּאִינוּן קְרֵבִין לְאוֹרַח מְהֵימְנוּתָא כְּווָתֵיהּ.

— The explanation is the teaching in Zohar Chadash, Yitro (D.V., 38a, end): “‘Radiance surrounds him’—this is the kingdom of Greece, which surrounds them as nogah,” and so forth, “for among all kingdoms none is as close to the path of faith as it.”
וּכְנֶגֶד זֶה גִּלְעָד שֶׁהוּא בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ וְקָרוֹב לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל נוֹגַהּ לוֹ סָבִיב.
— Corresponding to this is Gilead, outside the Land but near the Land of Israel: “Radiance surrounds him.”

וְיַעֲקֹב תִּקְּנוֹ שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ גַּלְעֵד הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (סִפְרֵי בְּרָכָה) עַל פָּסוּק וַיַּרְאֵהוּ וְגוֹמֵר אֶת הַגִּלְעָד מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהֶרְאָהוּ בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְכוּלֵי וְאֵין גִּלְעָד אֶלָּא בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (יִרְמְיָהוּ כ״ב:ו׳) גִּלְעָד אַתָּה לִי רֹאשׁ הַלְּבָנוֹן.

— Jacob’s rectifying it by naming it Gal-ed follows the Sifrei on Berakhah: “‘He showed him,’ and so forth, ‘Gilead’—this teaches that He showed him the Temple,” and so forth. “Gilead” means the Temple, as it says, “You are Gilead to Me, the summit of Lebanon” (Jeremiah 22:6).

p: וְזֶה שֶׁתִּקְּנוֹ יַעֲקֹב וְהִכְנִיסוֹ לִקְדוּשָּׁה שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב תִּיקֵּן קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה כָּל דִּבְרֵי רְשׁוּת וְיַעֲקֹב הִכְנִיס כָּל דִּבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת לִקְדוּשָּׁה,
— Jacob rectified it and brought it into holiness: he rectified kelippat nogah, the source of all optional activities, and brought all such activities into holiness.
שֶׁלֹּא יָדַע כְּלָל מֵהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ דְּכָל עוֹבָדוֹי הֲווֹ לִשְׁמָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
— He knew nothing of self-gratification, for all his deeds were for the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, as stated in the holy Zohar.

וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ דְּיִשַׁי מֵת בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ דִּמְפָרֵשׁ בֵּיהּ קְרָא (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שַׁבָּת נה:) שֶׁהוּא לְהַרְגִּישׁ הֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ שֶׁעַל יִשַׁי נֶאֱמַר הֵן בְּעָווֹן חוֹלָלְתִּי וְאָמְרוּ (מִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ) בְּעָווֹן מָלֵא וְכוּלֵי חָסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ צַד אֶחָד מֵעָוֹן וְכוּלֵי,

— We have explained that Yishai died through the serpent’s counsel, as Scripture explicitly indicates (Shabbat 55b), meaning the sensation of self-gratification. Concerning Yishai it says, “Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity.” The Midrash Rabbah at the beginning of Tazria comments, “The word be-avon is written in full,” and so forth: even the most pious of the pious cannot be entirely without some trace of iniquity, and so forth.
וְהַיְינוּ הֶרְגֵּשׁ הֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ,
— This is the sensation of self-gratification.

וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר מַה שֶּׁקַּל שֶׁבַּקַּלִּים אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר כֵּן אֶלָּא לְהוֹלִיד תּוֹלָדוֹת אָמַר כָּךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב פֵּרוּשׁ רַבִּי שְׁלֹמֹה יִצְחָקִי (וַיֵּצֵא מִבְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה),

— Yet Jacob our father, peace be upon him, said something that even the most frivolous person would not say, solely for the sake of producing offspring, as Rashi explains in Vayetzei, citing Bereishit Rabbah.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יָדַע כְּלָל מֵהֲנָאַת הַגּוּף רַק כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד לֵב בָּשָׂר לֵב לְהוֹצִיא בָּשָׂר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א׳ קלז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳),
— He knew nothing of bodily pleasure, but was as people will be in the future: “a heart of flesh,” a heart directed toward bringing forth flesh, as stated in Midrash Haneelam (Zohar I, 137b, end).
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא יָדַע בּוּשָׁה בָּזֶה כְּמוֹ קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל דִּכְתִיב וְלֹא יִתְבּוֹשָׁשׁוּ.
— He therefore felt no shame in this, as before the primordial corruption, when “they were not ashamed.”
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁלֹּא יָדַע כְּלָל מֵהֲנָאַת הַגּוּף שֶׁהוּא עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ עַל כֵּן יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ לֹא מֵת (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב תַּעֲנִית ה:),
— Since he knew nothing of bodily gratification, the serpent’s counsel, “Jacob our father did not die” (as stated in Taanit 5b).
וְהִכְנִיס גִּלְעָד שֶׁהִיא קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ לִקְדוּשָּׁה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כִּקְדוּשַּׁת בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
— He brought Gilead, kelippat nogah, into holiness, giving it the sanctity of the Temple.

וְכֵן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ קִידֵּשׁ גַּם כֵּן כָּל דְּבַר הָרְשׁוּת שֶׁהוּא מִקְּלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ וְלֹא מֵת גַּם כֵּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סוֹטָה יג:) וְלָכֵן וַיַּרְאֵהוּ אֶת הַגִּלְעָד זֶה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ.

— Likewise, Moses our teacher sanctified every optional activity, which derives from kelippat nogah, and likewise did not die, as stated in Sotah 13b. Hence, “‘He showed him Gilead’—this is the Temple.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Tanya, Likutei Amarim, chapter 7: “It [kelippat nogah] is an intermediate level between the three completely impure kelippot and the level and degree of holiness. Therefore, at times it is included within the three impure kelippot, as stated in Etz Chayim, Gate 49, beginning of chapter 4, in the name of the Zohar. At other times it is included in holiness and rises to its level: this occurs when the good mixed within it is separated from the evil, prevails, ascends, and becomes included in holiness. For example, someone eats rich beef and drinks fragrant wine to broaden his mind for God and His Torah—as Rava said, “Wine and fragrance, etc.”—or to fulfill the mitzvah of delighting in Shabbat and festivals. Then the vitality of the meat and wine, which had flowed from kelippat nogah, is refined and rises to God like a burnt offering and a sacrifice.”

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 55b: “The Gemara raises an objection from what was taught in the following baraita: Four people died due to Adam’s sin with the serpent, in the wake of which death was decreed upon all of mankind, although they themselves were free of sin. And they are: Benjamin, son of Jacob; Amram, father of Moses; Yishai, father of David; and Kilab, son of David. And all of them were learned through tradition, except for Yishai, father of David, with regard to whom there is an explicit verse interpreted homiletically, as it is written: ‘And Absalom placed Amasa in charge of the army in place of Joab, and Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra the Israelite, who had taken to himself Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, the mother of Joab’ (II Samuel 17:25).”

paragraphs.text: Vayikra Rabbah 14:5: “Another matter, ‘when a woman conceives’ – that is what is written: ‘I was generated in iniquity (Psalms 51:7). Rabbi Aḥa said: Even if one would be the most pious of the pious, it is impossible that he will not have one aspect of iniquity. David said before the Holy One blessed be He: ‘Master of the universe, did my father Yishai intend to produce me; was his intention not for his pleasure? Know that it is so, for after they have fulfilled their needs, this one turns his face to here and that one turns her face to there, and you insert each and every drop that is in him.’ That is what David said: ‘For my father and my mother have forsaken me, but the Lord will take me’ (Psalms 27:10). ‘In sin my mother conceived me’ (Psalms 51:7). Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said: A woman conceives only after her menstrual period and proximate to it, especially if it is a male. That is what is written: ‘When a woman conceives and bears a male child.’”

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 137b, Midrash Haneelam (Toldot 6:55–56): “Rabbi Acha bar Yaakov said: Come and see what is written: “Isaac entreated the Lord on behalf of his wife, for she was barren.” Why was she barren? Because the evil inclination is not present in its power in the world; thus procreation is not found except through prayer. What is written? “The Lord answered his entreaty, and Rebecca his wife conceived.” When the inclination is aroused, procreation becomes possible. Rabbi Yosei said: If so, what difference is there between this world and that future time? Moreover, Scripture says that the Holy One, blessed be He, will do this. Rabbi Acha answered: Indeed, the Holy One, blessed be He, will arouse that impulse which is needed for union. It will not remain constantly with a person as now, when it is always present and people sin through it; it will arise solely for that union, and its awakening will come from the Holy One, blessed be He. This is “I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.” What is “a heart of flesh”? Rabbi Yehudah said: A heart for bringing forth flesh, and for no other purpose.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Lag BaOmer 8:2: “Of Jacob we find in the holy Zohar, ‘Because he ascended into the World to Come.’ For Jacob our father was like Adam before the sin. He said what even the most frivolous person would not say, for he intended only to bring forth offspring, as stated in the Midrash Rabbah and in Rashi on Vayeitzei; that is, he knew nothing at all of self-gratification, like Adam before the sin, of whom it says, ‘They were not ashamed.’ Therefore it is taught, ‘Jacob our father did not die.’ So too Moses our teacher: it is taught in the Tikkunim, ‘Moses was there, but from the inner side; this one from the body and this one from the soul,’ so he was the inner aspect of Jacob our father and merited Binah, the World to Come. Moses our teacher too knew no evil at all, and it is taught, ‘When Moses was born, the whole house was filled with light’: the primordial light, the light that ‘was good,’ which was hidden away.”

h: Knowing the Creator and Revealing Elijah

p: וְאִיתָא מֵרַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ מִלּוּבְלִין זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה עַל פָּסוּק וּלְמָכִיר נָתַתִּי אֶת הַגִּלְעָד לְמַכִּיר בּוֹרְאוֹ נָתַתִּי אֶת הַגִּלְעָד זֶה אֵלִיָּהוּ,
— Our holy teacher of Lublin, of blessed and holy memory, taught concerning “To Machir I gave Gilead”: “To one who recognizes his Creator, I give Gilead”—this is Eliyahu.

וְכַוָּנָתוֹ עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (פְּסָחִים סח.) גִּלְעָד זֶה אֵלִיָּהוּ וְכוּלֵי שֶׁאֵלִיָּהוּ גַּם כֵּן קִידֵּשׁ דְּבַר הָרְשׁוּת שֶׁהוּא מִקְּלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ וְלֹא יָדַע כְּלָל מֵהֲנָאַת הַגּוּף שֶׁהוּא עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ וְעוֹדֶנּוּ בַּחַיִּים וְכֵן כָּתוּב (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כז) כְּבָר הָיָה אֵלִיָּהוּ שֶׁלֹּא חָטָא הוּא חַי וְקַיָּם לְעוֹלָם.

— He refers to the teaching, “‘Gilead’—this is Eliyahu,” and so forth (Pesachim 68a). Eliyahu too sanctified optional activity, derived from kelippat nogah, and knew nothing of bodily gratification, the serpent’s counsel; he remains alive. Likewise, Vayikra Rabbah 27 states, “Eliyahu already existed: since he did not sin, he lives and endures forever.”
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לְמַכִּיר בּוֹרְאוֹ הַיְינוּ מִי שֶׁזָּכָה לִבְחִינַת הַדַּעַת וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה נָשֹׂא רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה י׳) דַּעַת זֶה הַמַּכִּיר אֶת בּוֹרְאוֹ.
— “To one who recognizes his Creator” means one who has attained daat, spiritual knowledge, as stated in Midrash Rabbah, Naso, beginning of chapter 10: “Knowledge is one who recognizes his Creator.”

נָתַתִּי אֶת הַגִּלְעָד שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְגִילּוּי אֵלִיָּהוּ שֶׁזֶּה גַּם כֵּן מַדְרֵיגָה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא דַּעַת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב רַבִּי שְׁלֹמֹה יִצְחָקִי תִּשָּׂא וּבְדַעַת רוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ.
— “I give Gilead”—he merits a revelation of Eliyahu, also a level of Divine inspiration, which is daat, as Rashi explains in Ki Tisa: “‘And with knowledge’—Divine inspiration.”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר נֵצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (עֵירוּבִין מג.) לָאו אֵלִיָּהוּ אֲמָרִינְהוּ וְכוּלֵי דִּלְמָא יוֹסֵף שֵׁידָא אֲמָרִינְהוּ,
— As the book Netzach Yisrael explains concerning Eruvin 43a: “Was it not Eliyahu who stated them?” and so forth; “Perhaps Joseph the demon stated them.”

שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי לֹא רָאוּ הָאוֹמֵר שֶׁאָז לֹא נִסְתַּפְּקוּ בְּסָפֵק זֶה רַק שֶׁהוֹפִיעוּ הַהֲלָכוֹת בְּלֵב אֶחָד מִבֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ וְלֹא יָדְעוּ אִם הָיָה מִצַּד הַקְּדוּשָּׁה עַל יְדֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ בִּבְחִינַת רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ אוֹ מִצַּד יוֹסֵף שֵׁידָא.

— Certainly they had not seen the speaker, for then they would not have entertained this doubt. Rather, the halakhot arose in the heart of someone in the study hall, and they did not know whether they came from holiness, through Eliyahu as Divine inspiration, or from Joseph the demon.

h: The Sanctity of the Shabbat Meal

p: וְזֶה עִנְיַן סְעוּדַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁעָשָׂה בְּגִלְעָד שֶׁעָשָׂה אוֹתוֹ כִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְהַזְּבָחִים מֵעֵין קְדוּשַּׁת קָרְבָּנוֹת וַהֲוֵי סְעוּדַת מִצְוָה סְעוּדָתָא דְּמַלְכָּא.

— This was the meaning of Jacob’s feast in Gilead: he endowed the place with the Temple’s sanctity, and the sacrifices with a sanctity resembling the Temple offerings. It was a commanded feast, the King’s feast.
וּבְשַׁבָּת בִּסְעוּדָה שְׁלִישִׁית שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ יְכוֹלִים לִזְכּוֹת לְקַדֵּשׁ כָּל דִּבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה.
— At the third Shabbat meal, corresponding to Jacob our father’s sanctity, one can merit to sanctify all optional activities, bringing them into holiness.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Sukkot 12:2: “With Abraham our father we find that he made a feast and rejoiced when his endeavors were clarified as being in complete holiness, as it says, ‘Abraham made a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.’ … With Isaac our father too we find that he made a meal of delicacies when his endeavors were clarified as rooted in holiness. … With Jacob, in whom was the complete general clarification, we do not find that he made a feast. One can say, however, that this too is alluded to when he parted from Laban, as it says, ‘Jacob offered a sacrifice and called his brothers to eat bread’: his sons, who were like brothers. For Jacob too needed clarification in his attribute, the attribute of truth, since all his dealings with Esau looked like a kind of deceit. … Outwardly, the clarification of Jacob’s attribute of truth was not complete until he parted from Laban and Laban acknowledged him; then the attribute of truth was clarified completely, as it says, ‘The lip of truth will be established forever.’ Then he called his brothers, his sons, to eat bread on the mound: this was the feast at the time when he and his sons were clarified in holiness and separated from all the nations, for the mound served to separate the Land of Israel from outside the Land.”
